title: [critic] Reduction Theorem: existence/regularity and escape-to-infinity of the coupling schedule are unproven

comments.author: critic-agent
comments.body:
**Gap in current `solution.tex`.** *Location:* Theorem "Reduction", hypothesis.

The Reduction Theorem assumes: "for every pair $P,Q$ there is a choice of nonnegative
relative speeds $\dot a,\dot b$ (not both zero), measurable along the flow, such that (S)
holds and such that the induced schedule reaches $a,b\to\infty$." It then chooses, at each
time, speeds realizing (S) and concludes $D'\le0$.

Two unproven realizability claims are buried in this hypothesis, independent of whether (S)
holds pointwise:

1. **Assembly / regularity.** Pointwise existence of admissible $(\dot a(P,Q),\dot b(P,Q))$
   does NOT give a measurable, let alone $C^1$, schedule $t\mapsto(a(t),b(t))$ for which the
   chain-rule identity (D) is valid. (D) was derived assuming a $C^1$ schedule. One must
   solve the differential inclusion $(\dot a,\dot b)\in \mathcal A(P(t),Q(t))$ with
   $P=p\boxplus G_a$, $Q=q\boxplus G_b$, and verify a solution with the required regularity
   exists. This is not addressed.

2. **Escape to infinity.** The schedule must reach $a,b\to\infty$ (needed so that
   $D(\infty)$ is the relevant endpoint). Nothing rules out the admissible set
   $\mathcal A(P,Q)$ forcing, e.g., $\dot a=0$ once $P$ is near-Gaussian, stalling the flow
   at finite $a$. With only the constraint "not both zero", a schedule could converge to a
   finite $(a_\infty,b_\infty)$, in which case the endpoint identity is the wrong one.

In the classical Stam/Blachman proof these issues do not arise because the schedule is
**canonical** (relative speed $\propto$ running Fisher information), giving an explicit ODE
with a global solution escaping to infinity. The file never exhibits the finite free
analogue of this canonical schedule; (S) is left as an *abstract sufficient condition*
whose *dynamical realizability* is unverified.

**Relation to other issues.** This is logically distinct from the inequality (S) itself
(the score-projection content, tracked in q4-47/q4-52) and from the endpoint circularity /
additivity-of-$C$ gap (q4-58). It concerns the existence and global behavior of the
coupling schedule.

**Suggested fix.** Either (a) exhibit the canonical schedule explicitly — e.g. speeds
$\dot a:\dot b = $ a specific ratio in $g(P),g(Q)$ as in the classical case — and prove the
resulting ODE has a global solution with $a,b\to\infty$; or (b) replace the dynamical
reduction by the static Blachman optimization, which avoids schedules entirely.
